newsitem.title: USA: Vons, Safeway takeover target, posts higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Vons, Safeway takeover target, posts higher profits.

text.p: The Vons Companies Inc., the supermarket chain that is a takeover target of Safeway Inc., said Thursday that its profits soared by almost 60 percent in the third quarter on higher sales and improved margins.

Vons, which said it was considering Safeway's unsolicited $1.68 billion stock offer for the Vons shares it does not own, said its net income for the sixteen-week period ended Oct. 6 jumped 59 percent to $29.4 million, or 66 cents a share, from $18.5 million, or 42 cents a share.
The company's stock, which jumped $11.25 to $54.375 Wednesday after Safeway announced its bid, added another $1.25 to $55.625 in Thursday morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

A combination of Vons and Safeway, which already owns about a third of Vons' stock, would create the second-biggest grocery store chain in the country, with 1,375 stores in 16 states and five Canadian provinces.

Vons, one of the largest supermarket chains in southern California, said that despite operating seven fewer stores, its sales in the quarter increased 7.1 percent to $1.68 billion from $1.57 billion. However, sales at stores opened for more than a year grew by only 5.2 percent, it said.

The company, which operates 322 stores under the Vons and Pavilions names, said its gross margin in the quarter improved to 25.1 percent of sales from 25.0 percent, which it said resulted from increased private brand sales and a reduction in costs as a percent of sales.

Vons said its selling and administrative expenses fell to 20.7 percent of sales from 21.2 percent, primarily due to a more efficient mix of store labour and productivity gains as well as continued efforts to control expenses.
"We continue to aggressively pursue opportunities to reduce our operating expenses without compromising our commitment to customer service," Chairman Lawrence A. Del Santo said in a statement.

"While some of these gains have been reinvested in store service levels and promotional programmes, we are pleased with the progress we have made in reducing our overall cost structure," Del Santo added.

The company, based in Arcadia, Calif., said its operating cash flow -- income before depreciation and amortization -- improved to 6.3 percent of sales from 6.0 percent. It also said its interest expense declined by 17 percent to $16.6 million from $20.1 million.

Vons also reiterated that a committee of outside directors was studying Safeway's proposal, announced Wednesday, to acquire Vons for $1.68 billion worth of Safeway stock and the assumption of $550 million in Vons debt.
While the Safeway offer sent Vons stock flying, at least some of its stockholders were not pleased with the proposal.
A group of shareholders filed a lawsuit late Wednesday seeking to block the takeover, claiming that a deal would be unfair to Vons' shareholders.
The purported class action suit, filed in Los Angeles, alleges that the "intrinsic value" of Vons exceeds the $58 a share offer by Safeway in light of Vons' potential growth and profitability.
Vons made no comment on the suit Thursday.

The company said its net income for the 40 weeks ended Oct. 6 rose 49 percent to $69.6 million, or $1.56 a share, from $47.0 million, or $1.07 a share, as sales expanded to $4.14 billion from $3.85 billion.
